But the prompt stack (Pick a landmark, 5 cities can build, Ruler points, +2 more) plus Choose production for 18 cities makes each turn feel like busywork. A 'skip/auto all' choice for the minor prompts would make late game turns move faster.

args.summary: Session summary (saves at turns 331 and 472). What works: the glossary (hold a readout for its entry, then an index with categories and search), save, load and continue are fast and clear, pinch and pan are smooth, and the army card is clear about supply, fortify, March and Hold. March mode shows a good hint bar ("tap a city or a tile to march to") with a Path option. Problems: (1) Bug: a tap on the X of the full screen tip also reaches the map and opens a tile card. This happened on three saves. (2) The Buy button does not show when I can't afford something, and it doesn't say how many turns until I can. (3) The tech tree takes too many scrolls to find one tech. (4) In the late game, prompts (landmarks, cities can build, ruler points, production for 18 cities) make each turn feel like busywork, so an auto or skip choice would help. I ran out of steps here, so in this session I did not finish the sea transport landing, the battles (one by hand, one on Auto) or the event cards. Fun 3/5,

args.summary: Information age session (turn 618). What worked: Escape closes the full screen tip cleanly, so no tap reaches the map. Buying is clear: the Guided-Missile Destroyer cost 1592, a confirm box showed the cost and when it would finish, and gold dropped from 1984 to 392. Advisor builds queued all 5 idle cities in one tap, which saves a lot of late game busywork. End Turn shows a "The world moves..." progress bar. Still open from earlier sessions: a tap on the tip's X also reaches the map, the Buy button doesn't show when I can't afford something, the tech tree needs too many scrolls, and the late game has a heavy stack of prompts (landmarks, ruler points, governors). Not finished, because I ran out of steps: landing an army by sea, one battle by hand and one on Auto, and the event cards. Fun 3/5, frustration 1 to 2.
